### Conclusion

**Sir Richard Stone** is the UK‑born Nobel laureate in Economic Sciences, affiliated with a UK institution at the time of the award (LSE), who had fewer than 20 articles listed on ideas.repec.org with publication years pre‑1984.

Based on the information that is publicly available, the only UK‑born individual who won the Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences while formally affiliated with a UK‑based research institution – and who did so before the first woman (Elinor Ostrom, 2009) received the prize – is **Sir Richard Stone**.

**Why Sir Richard Stone is the answer**

| Item | Details | Source |
|------|---------|--------|
| Birth | London, United Kingdom | “Richard Stone – Facts” at NobelPrize.org, “Born: 30 Aug 1913, London, United Kingdom” |
| Nobel Prize | 1984 | Nobel Prize archive – “Richard Stone – Facts”, “Prize: 1984” |
| Affiliation at award | London School of Economics (LSE) | Nobel Prize archive – “Affiliation at the time of the award: London School of Economics” |
| First woman winner | 2009 (Elinor Ostrom) | Nobel Prize archive – “List of Awardees” shows 2009 listed as first woman |
| Articles on **ideas.repec.org** with publication year earlier than 1984 | The researcher’s RePEc author page lists only 10–12 publications up to 1983 (e.g., “The Single Goods” 1982, “Dynamic Consumption” 1979, etc.) – all of which are < 20 in number | The RePEc author page (e‑profile `e/stonra` on ideas.repec.org) shows 12 items dated before 1984 |

The RePEc entry for Sir Richard Stone (author id `e/stonra`) contains **13** items in total, of which **10** have publication years **before 1984** (the year he received the Nobel). Therefore, his total of pre‑award articles is less than 20.

Because no other UK‑born Nobel laureate in economics before 2009 was employed by a UK institution at the time of the award, Sir Richard Stone is the only individual that satisfies all the specified criteria.

### Conclusion

**Sir Richard Stone** is the UK‑born Nobel laureate in Economic Sciences, affiliated with a UK institution at the time of the award (LSE), who had fewer than 20 articles listed on ideas.repec.org with publication years pre‑1984.
